entries.title: II Chronicles 25:2
segments:
He did that which was right; externally, and for a time. 
 
Many for a time do that externally which is right, who have no supreme regard to God, and whose services for this reason are not accepted of him.

entries.title: II Chronicles 25:5
segments: When men engage in projects without asking counsel of the Lord, they may expect them to be sources of trouble, if not of ruin.

entries.title: II Chronicles 25:6
segments: He hired also a hundred thousand mighty men; to assist him in a war which he proposed against the Edomites.

entries.title: II Chronicles 25:7
segments: Men, out of regard to their own interests merely, sometimes do externally as the Lord directs, and thus save themselves from many of the evils which would otherwise come upon them.

entries.title: II Chronicles 25:9
segments: Men are often very reluctant to do what is right, on account of the pecuniary sacrifice it may involve; but whatever be the sacrifice it may involve; but whatever be the sacrifice which obedience to God may occasion, it is wise to make it, for God can give us much more than we lose for his sake.

entries.title: II Chronicles 25:12
segments: Unto the top of the rock; the word in the original for rock is Sela, the same as that used in

.  Sela is generally considered to have been the same as Petra, (rock,) a celebrated city of Edom lying in a valley surrounded by precipices of rock, from which it received its name. 
 
Apostasy and cruelty are often united.  War tends to the production and increase of both, and is a source of innumerable evils to mankind.

entries.title: II Chronicles 25:14
segments: That men who know the true God and have received special blessings from him, should renounce his service, bow down to idols, and expect to be gainers by it, shows that the heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately wicked.

entries.title: II Chronicles 25:16
segments: When men persevere in rejecting the counsel of God, it is evidence that he intends to destroy them.

entries.title: II Chronicles 25:17
segments: Let us see one another; let us try our strength together in battle. On this whole narrative,

, and the notes upon that passage. 
 
As a punishment for their sins, God often suffers the wicked, in gratification of their pride, to engage in projects which occasion their ruin.

entries.title: II Chronicles 25:27
segments: Turning away from the Lord is often followed by great troubles from men, who, though they mean not so, neither does their heart think so, are yet instrumental in executing the wrath of God upon those who rebel against him.
